themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in Washington Heights
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 1.0 per week—an 800% increase (z-score: 4.82)—signaling a possible sudden concentration of street homelessness or inadequate shelter access in CD 112.
evidence: 9 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.82 indicates statistically significant spike
Community board budget requests show repeated demand for park safety and security staff enhancement, suggesting chronic homelessness visibility
reporting_angles: On-the-ground tour of encampments: where are they concentrated? Are they new or expanding?
Interview DHS/Parks on why spike occurred this week—did a shelter close, or did enforcement push populations to CD 112?

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement crackdown escalates
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.8 per week—a 471% spike (z-score: 5.28)—suggesting either aggressive new enforcement action or concentrated street vending complaints in a specific area.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.28 indicates high statistical significance
No recent news coverage suggests story has not been picked up citywide yet
reporting_angles: NYPD Vendor Enforcement Bureau activity: is there a new sweep operation in Washington Heights or Inwood?
Street vendor interviews: are they being targeted unfairly or is there legitimate quality-of-life enforcement?

themes_detail.label: Public urination complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—pointing to either a specific location of concern, homeless population concentration, or lack of public restroom access.
evidence: 3 public urination complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Convergence with encampment spike (9 complaints THIS WEEK) suggests homeless population concentration
reporting_angles: Identify the specific block or blocks where complaints are clustered—geographic concentration is key
Check whether public restroom availability in these areas is adequate; tie to broader city restroom access story

themes_detail.label: Asbestos hazard cluster detected
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 433% spike (z-score: 4.91)—likely indicating a construction project or building renovation releasing asbestos or residents discovering hazards in aging housing stock.
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.91 indicates high statistical significance
378 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (329 alterations) creates exposure risk in dense neighborhood
reporting_angles: Identify which building(s) or construction sites triggered asbestos complaints—cross-reference with DOB permit database
Broader investigation: how many pre-1980s residential buildings in CD 112 have been tested or remediated for asbestos?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/vaping in residential buildings rises
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or Vaping complaints increased to 9 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 4.2 per week—a 112% spike (z-score: 3.96)—indicating possible violation of smoke-free housing rules or tenant disputes over secondhand smoke exposure.
evidence: 9 smoking/vaping complaints last week vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Part of broader noise and quality-of-life complaint cluster (residential noise at 2,673 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are NYCHA buildings involved, or is this private rental housing?
Interview residents on enforcement: how accessible is smoke-free housing complaint process and how quickly do buildings respond?
